Messages.Author: Nicx
Messages.Body:
Hi,

Here the situation: Vamp A have 1 blood on him. Vamp A play a Forced
Awekening and block Vamp B. Vamp B play Psychomania superior...

Does Vamp A burn 1 blood for the fail block and go to torpor from the
1 damage of Psychomania? Thanks!

Nicolas Savard
Domain Saguenay

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Nicx wrote:
> Here the situation: Vamp A have 1 blood on him. Vamp A play a Forced
> Awekening and block Vamp B. Vamp B play Psychomania superior...
>
> Does Vamp A burn 1 blood for the fail block and go to torpor from the
> 1 damage of Psychomania? Thanks!

Psychomachia can only be played if the block is successful, so FA's
non-blocking penalty won't be applied.

Messages.Author: Marc Gabriele
Messages.Body:
On Thu, 28 Aug 2003, LSJ wrote:

> Psychomachia can only be played if the block is successful, so FA's
> non-blocking penalty won't be applied.

Is there any wiggle room in the timing between when the block is
initially declared successful and when Psychomachia is played to order any
other effects that may occur due to a successful block? For example, must
the blocking minion tap? Must Millicent Smith activate? Or is it up to the
acting player's discretion?

Marc G.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


Psychomachia is played before the blocking minion is tapped for the successful
block.

Millicent would activate before Psychomachia (or Change of Target or Obedience
or whatever) could be played.


